notes.detailedSummary: The supplied sources support singular weighted dbar solutions, point extension with constants independent of m/u on fixed domains, multiplier-ideal coherence and nonzero stalks, coherent-section topology, Cartan B and Fréchet openness. notes.text:
Essential-source verdict: PASS for the main iff theorem through the directly supplied Demailly route. No author or ROOT mathematical conclusion was granted. The absent original Hörmander1965/1990, OT1987, Nadel1990, GR84 and Nar66 editions are not claimed read. DEL and strong openness remain disclosed published auxiliary imports whose original editions are absent; neither enters the main iff.

Required whole units were displayed and assessed using literal LF splitting with formfeeds retained: agbook VIII6.5 LF21001–21054, whole6.9 LF21061–21118; IX1.3–1.5 LF22508–22568; section4.C LF23507–23565 and its continuation23566–23606; entire4.7 LF23607–23652; IX4.10/4.11 and the complete ensuing proof LF23714–23882. OT whole4.11/4.12 LF830–865, whole6.1 LF1106–1171, whole7.1–7.3 LF1448–1495 were read. Additionally, the complete q=0 theorem4.1 and proof/remarks LF372–763 were read, including its approximate-equation and regularity cases. Bourbaki whole2.4.4 LF503–522 was read in text and PDFpage11 because OCR omits formulas. OT PDFpage15 was viewed to confirm section, determinant and logarithmic factors. No whole-PDF visual-reading claim is made.

H: VIII6.5 gives the inverse-curvature-eigenvalue estimate for weighted (n,q)-forms on weakly pseudoconvex Kähler manifolds. Its proof applies the weighted metric, exhausts the manifold and takes weak limits. Conversion to (0,q)-forms adds Ricci curvature, which vanishes on Euclidean balls. The singular-weight application follows the whole6.9 regularization argument. On smaller balls, radial smoothings W_t decrease to W and preserve a strict Hessian lower bound. Data norms against exp(-W_t) are bounded by their original norm. Compact upper bounds on W_t give local unweighted L² bounds for solutions. Diagonal weak limits solve dbar h=a. First pass estimates against a fixed regularized weight, then decrease that weight to W and exhaust the domain. Weak lower semicontinuity and MCT give the limiting estimate.

Numeric1 is unnecessary. Directly6.9 with epsilon=1 and q=1 gives integral(1+|z|²)^(-1)|h|² exp(-W) ≤4 integral(1+|z|²)|a|² exp(-W). Consequently C_D=4(1+sup_D|z|²)^2 bounds the ordinary W-weighted solution norm by the data norm on bounded D. This explicit geometric constant is independent of m,u and is absorbed in the transfer constants. Both applications use W=m(u+rho)+(n+q)log|z-x|²+|z|², q≥0. These weights are psh; cutoff derivatives avoid x; germ or source-section integrability makes their data norms finite. Since W-m(u+rho) is bounded above on D, the solution also has the original Hilbert norm. Smooth data do not mean a smooth weight.

O: In OT4.11 use the flat rank-n bundle and s(z)=(z-x)/(e d), d=diam D, Y={x}. It is transverse and |s|≤e^(-1). Bundle curvature is zero. The q=0 theorem4.1 applies with alpha=1 because the scalar psh weight W and n log|s|² have nonnegative complex Hessians. Its determinant factor |Lambda^n ds|² is a fixed Euclidean metric factor times (e d)^(-2n). If M_n=max_{0<t≤e^(-1)}t^(2n)(-log t)^2, then4.11 implies integral_D|F|² exp(-W) ≤C_n M_n(e d)^(2n) exp(-W(x)), F(x)=1, with fixed norm/volume factors absorbed. Thus precisely the required fixed-domain geometric constant is independent of W,x, hence m,u. Converting scalar functions to trivialized holomorphic n-forms introduces only these fixed factors. A fixed quadratic used for strictness changes the bound geometrically.

The isolated C_n display in4.12 does not justify a constant uniform under arbitrary domain rescaling; its printed diameter dependence is not used for that inference. The bound just derived from4.11 has the appropriate geometric dependence. For singular W,4.11 explicitly allows psh weights. Its regularization application can also be reconstructed: apply q=0 extension on increasing smaller domains with W_t↓W; at finite-valued x the norm bound is at most C_D exp(-W(x)). Local normal compactness preserves F(x)=1, and estimates against fixed regularized weights followed by Fatou/MCT recover the singular-weight norm. At W(x)=-infinity only 0≤K_W(x) is used. The source's4.9c treats the approximate equation through a minimal solution and ellipticity. No positive-degree Manivel regularity conjecture is applied. Bourbaki's projective-family OT4.3.1 is not used as the point theorem. Whole OT6.1 separately confirms the kernel lower and mean-value upper estimates in the half-weight convention; only compact-subset normal convergence is used.

N: OT7.1 defines ideals through |f|² exp(-2phi); take phi=m(u+rho)/2. Whole7.3 proves coherence using the strongly Noetherian ideal generated by weighted global sections, point-pole jet approximation and Krull separation. Bourbaki2.4.4 contains the same proof, with its missing OCR weight visible on PDFpage11: phi+(n+s)log|z-x|+|z|². Nonzero stalks are checked separately: a nontrivial psh weight on a connected ball is finite somewhere; O extends value1 there with finite weighted norm. That nonzero holomorphic function has a nonzero germ at every point by the identity theorem, even where its value vanishes. All its germs lie in the ideal. Smooth bounded changes of weight preserve integrability by two-sided positive constants.

C: IX1.3 proves Krull separation with Artin–Rees/Nakayama;1.5 proves that finitely generated submodules are closed in analytic Krull topology and have the induced topology. Compact-open convergence implies convergence of germ jets by Cauchy estimates. Therefore coherent ideal sections are closed in O(V). Section4.C constructs the natural Fréchet topology through local quotient presentations and compatible closed families; whole4.7 proves continuity of coherent maps and closedness of coherent subspaces. The inclusion J(V)→O(V) is continuous and bijective onto a closed compact-open Fréchet subspace. Fréchet open mapping makes its inverse continuous. Thus natural and induced topologies agree.

For a finite generating map O^s→J on a product of balls, the kernel is coherent. The product has the strictly psh proper exhaustion -log(r²-|z|²)-log(r²-|w|²), so it is strongly1-complete. IX4.11 gives H¹(kernel)=0, and the exact cohomology sequence gives global coefficient-map surjectivity. Multiplication by fixed generators is continuous in compact seminorms; Fréchet openness therefore applies. The entire ensuing4.10 proof was checked: strongly q-convex bumps, Mayer–Vietoris, compact cochain restriction and finite-dimensional Hausdorff cohomology, dense q-1 restriction, then inverse-limit passage. This validates the application without recursively reproving all analytic foundations.

Additional needed units were checked: Artin–Rees/Nakayama and proofs LF22473–22506; coherent kernels and definitions LF4630–4743, Oka/strong Noetherian LF4750–4854; psh definitions, maxima, convolution, canonical distributions and envelopes LF1980–2099; mean values, connected L¹ dichotomy and recovery LF1683–1845; pluriharmonic real-part representation LF2162–2187; q-convex/complete definitions LF22800–22827 and22890–22903. Canonical positive-Hessian distributions have unique L¹ psh representatives by I5.8, proved through convolution. Psh values equal limits of shrinking ball averages: sub-mean gives one inequality and usc gives the other. Hence a.e. comparison of canonical psh functions implies pointwise comparison.

Exact local theta-potentials need no rationality or line bundle. Locally choose a real1-form S with dS=2pi theta. Dolbeault gives S^(0,1)=barpartial v, so dS=partialbarpartial(v-bar v)=i partialbarpartial(2 Im v). Thus rho=2 Im v is a smooth real dd^c-potential. Differences have zero complex Hessian and equal real parts of holomorphic functions on simply connected transfer balls. Source LF7286–7302 and14986–14993 corroborate this local construction; the extraction's Re/Im prose is not substituted for this algebra.

DPS whole LF404–775 was read, including2.2.1,2.2.2,Steps1–4 and2.2.13. It is contextual corroboration, not R. Its exp(-2phi), local1/(2m) and i partialbarpartial conventions require phi=u/2: pi theta+i partialbarpartial(u/2)=pi(theta+dd^c u), and source loss epsilon becomes epsilon/pi. Step3 fixes a cover; Step4 changes covers/loss and takes tails. Remark2.2.2 warns that final equisingular approximants need not retain logarithmic poles. None supplies the candidate's fixed-cover exact finite norms or relative constant2.

notes.summary: Sufficiency proved for every real c: canonical upper tails, uniform L¹ bounds, connected noncollapse, vanishing curvature loss and exact capped germ-integrability identity. No strong openness or mass premise.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite increasing maxima converge locally in L¹; positivity and average recovery identify the raw supremum almost everywhere with its usc representative. Nested compact upper-level sets and negative-integral propagation on fixed overlap balls yield a nontrivial decreasing canonical theta-psh limit. DCT in N and MCT in R then j establish the exact extended integral identity. Both germ directions preserve the required U/C/j/R/N quantifiers, null-set conventions and all-real indexing.
notes.text:
Use dd^c=i partialbarpartial/(2pi), connected compact Kähler X, Kähler omega and smooth closed real theta. The input is an arbitrary array of nonzero coherent ideals A_c for every real c>0, with no compatibility presumed. A permitted certificate has finite tuples generating exactly A_(2^j) on the prescribed inner compact balls, fixed known theta-potentials and radial quadratic barriers, explicit boundary gluing, and actual finite maxima Phi_j satisfying theta+dd^c Phi_j≥-epsilon_j omega, epsilon_j↓0, and -B≤sup_X Phi_j≤B. No unknown target or arbitrary correction is admitted.

These are canonical quasi-psh functions: each finite nonzero ideal norm is locally integrable, the known smooth terms preserve this, and the justified maximum gluing is local. Two tuples generating the same ideal express each other through holomorphic matrices; their squared norms are comparable on smaller compact neighborhoods, including common zeros. A bounded correction describing the common ideal-norm type need not be continuous at zeros. Its regularity is never used for curvature; the actual branches supply the curvature checks.

For fixed j set H_(j,N)=max_(j≤k≤N)Phi_k. Adding a local smooth potential of theta+epsilon_j omega makes every later branch psh because epsilon_k≤epsilon_j, hence makes H_(j,N) psh. The sequence increases, is ≤B and ≥Phi_j. Thus a constant plus |Phi_j| dominates its absolute value locally, and DCT gives local L¹ convergence to S_j=sup_(k≥j)Phi_k. Positivity passes distributionally. Let v_j be the canonical quasi-psh representative of this distribution.

Each H_(j,N)≤v_j a.e. implies the inequality everywhere by adding the same smooth potential and recovering psh values from shrinking averages. Therefore S_j≤v_j and S_j*≤v_j. Conversely, averages of S_j plus that potential equal averages of v_j plus the potential. They are bounded by local suprema of S_j plus the potential; shrink the ball to obtain v_j≤S_j*. Hence Psi_j=S_j*=v_j=S_j a.e., and theta+dd^c Psi_j≥-epsilon_j omega. Canonical representatives agree on overlaps. Countability allows one volume-null exceptional set for all j.

Uniform L¹ bounds independent of j,N can also be established. All Phi_j have the common lower curvature eta=theta+epsilon_1 omega and attain a value at least-B at some x_j. Subdivide a fixed inner chart cover into finitely many small cells. For each cell choose an anchor ball lying inside a fixed-radius ball about every point of the cell, while that larger ball stays in the chart. Add eta's smooth potential. Sub-mean at x_j bounds the negative integral on the ball centered there, hence on its fixed anchor. There are finitely many possible anchors. Fixed overlap chains from each anchor to a finite target cover propagate the bounds as described below. Thus all Phi_j have a common global L¹ bound; Phi_j≤H_(j,N)≤B gives the same bound for every finite maximum.

The Psi_j decrease, are ≤B, and have suprema at least-B. K_j={Psi_j≥-B-1} are nonempty nested compact sets: usc attains the finite supremum, and X is compact. Choose x0 in their intersection. The pointwise decreasing limit p satisfies p(x0)≥-B-1.

Here is explicit negative-integral propagation. On each relatively compact large chart add a fixed smooth potential sigma of eta. Then v_j=Psi_j+sigma are decreasing psh and have a common upper bound M. Their values at x0 have a common lower bound. Sub-mean gives integral_(ball centered x0)(M-v_j)≤Vol(ball)(M-v_j(x0)). Suppose a fixed positive-volume compact overlap ball E has such a bound K. Changing potentials alters the bound only by a fixed constant. For every j there is y_j in E with v'_j(y_j)≥M'-K/Vol(E), with an arbitrarily enlarged K if needed. Choose E small enough that a fixed-radius ball about every y in E stays in the next large chart and contains a fixed next small ball T. Sub-mean at y_j bounds the negative integral on that larger ball and therefore on T. Radii, volumes and potential differences are fixed; the chosen y_j may depend on j.

Arrange these choices along paths using successive small centers less than a quarter-radius apart and larger chart balls around them. At transitions choose E compactly inside both charts and reduce radii. A connected manifold is path connected. Compactness allows finitely many target balls and finitely many such chains from x0, so all local negative integrals are uniformly bounded. This establishes the required noncollapse propagation rather than assuming a decreasing-sequence dichotomy.

Now M-v_j increase with bounded integrals. MCT gives an integrable limit and L¹ convergence, locally and then globally. A decreasing limit of usc functions is usc. Passing sub-mean to the limit gives its inequality against ball averages; usc supplies the reverse shrinking-average inequality. Thus p is the exact canonical representative, not an arbitrary usc modification of its distribution. Equivalently the decreasing complex-line sub-mean inequalities make p+sigma psh. The finite value at x0 makes p nontrivial. Passing theta+epsilon_j omega+dd^c Psi_j≥0 in distributions, using L¹ convergence and epsilon_j→0, gives theta+dd^c p≥0. Therefore u=p belongs to PSH(X,theta).

Fix x, real c>0 and a germ f. Choose x in a relatively compact coordinate ball U with its representative holomorphic near closure U. For fixed j and integer R≥1, |f|² min{R,exp(-cH_(j,N))} decreases with N and is dominated by R|f|² in L¹(U). Its pointwise limit uses S_j. DCT and S_j=Psi_j a.e. yield
lim_N integral_U |f|² min{R,exp(-cH_(j,N))}=integral_U |f|² min{R,exp(-cPsi_j)}.
For fixed j, MCT in integer R gives the uncapped integral, possibly infinite. Since Psi_j↓u, another MCT in j gives
sup_(j,R) lim_N integral_U |f|² min{R,exp(-cH_(j,N))}=integral_U |f|² exp(-cu).
This is an extended-value identity; no ideal intersection is exchanged with a decreasing limit.

At a pole the capped exponential is R; simultaneous zeros of f contribute0 for every cap. Define the uncapped product through these increasing caps, avoiding 0 times infinity. Nontrivial psh poles have volume0 by local L¹ integrability. Smooth positive volumes and coordinate changes compare by bounded positive factors on smaller balls, so null-set conventions do not affect integrability.

Both germ directions now follow with exactly the stated quantifiers. If f belongs to A_(c,x), the certificate provides one U and finite C independent of all j,R. The identity bounds the full integral by C, so f belongs to I(cu)_x. Conversely, if f belongs to I(cu)_x, shrink its local integrability neighborhood to a ball U whose closure lies there. Take its finite full integral as C. Every capped tail integral is ≤C because Psi_j≥u; the certificate's iff puts f in A_(c,x). The zero germ is included. U,C may depend on x,c,f, but not j,R; N is taken with N≥j. No common ball or constant across different germs or exponents is required.

This proves sufficiency and equality A_c=I(cu) at EVERY real c>0, rather than just dyadic samples. It uses the ordinary foundations checked in n1, with no strong openness, subadditivity, mass premise or prior R. The raw output may depend on the witness. notes.summary: Independent R proof establishes exact finite prescribed-ideal norms, fixed-scale relative kernel reduction including zeros, exact-potential transfer/gluing and pointwise usc tail recovery at poles. Main iff PASS.
notes.detailedSummary: Point-pole dbar solutions, Artin–Rees/Nakayama and coherence give exact finite weighted Hilbert generation on fixed compact balls. Normal convergence and the coherent product ideal, together with topology identification, Cartan B and Fréchet openness, give P≤K≤2P; truncation can depend arbitrarily on m. Exact smooth theta-potentials cancel weights in transfer, so comparison constants are geometric and independent of m/u. Known radial barriers give explicit boundary domination and O(1/m) curvature loss. Locally uniform mean-value estimates and point-extension lower bounds prove exact upper-tail convergence everywhere and necessity for all real indices.
notes.text:
Use the ordinary H/O/N/C inputs independently checked in n1 and the envelope/integration results proved in n2. No R theorem is imported from DPS, working305 or another campaign. Let u be any nontrivial theta-psh function; no mass hypothesis is made. Fix once nested coordinate balls B_a^0⊂⊂B_a^1⊂⊂B_a^2⊂⊂B_a^3 whose cores cover X, coordinates defined beyond closure B_a^3, and known exact smooth rho_a with dd^c rho_a=theta. Choose core radii at most half the B_a^1 radii. These choices and their finite derivative/value/coordinate bounds are geometric.

On D=B_a^3 put v=u+rho_a, psh and nontrivial, and H_m={F holomorphic on D: integral_D|F|² exp(-mv)dλ<infinity}. Smooth bounded changes give I(mv)=I(mu) locally. Weighted L² convergence implies unweighted L² convergence on compact subsets because v is locally bounded above; distributional regularity makes the limit holomorphic. Hence H_m is complete. The weighted measure has finite density a.e. and is sigma finite by exhausting where the density is bounded, so H_m is separable. Point extension at a finite-valued point provides a nonzero member. Its germs are nonzero throughout connected D, including its zero values.

Exact generation: N makes I_x=I(mv)_x finite over the Noetherian holomorphic local ring. Artin–Rees gives q≥0 with I_x∩m_x^(q+1)⊂m_x I_x: if s is its index, choose q≥s and use I∩m^(q+1)=m^(q+1-s)(I∩m^s). For a finite local generator g of I_x, choose a representative on a small weighted-integrability neighborhood and a smooth cutoff chi supported there and equal1 near x. Solve on D
 dbar h=dbar(chi g), W=mv+(n+q)log|z-x|²+|z|².
The data are smooth, closed, supported away from x and finite-norm. H supplies a solution. W-mv is bounded above on bounded D, so h also has the original weighted norm. Near x it is holomorphic. Since v is locally bounded above, W-integrability implies integral|h|²|z-x|^(-2(n+q))<infinity. A first nonzero homogeneous Taylor term of degree k has a nonzero spherical squared integral and radial exponent2k-2q-1; integrability forces k>q. Thus h_x∈I_x∩m_x^(q+1). F=chi g-h is globally holomorphic, belongs to H_m and equals g modulo m_x I_x. Repeating for finite generators and applying Nakayama to the quotient proves exact generation at x. Coherence extends equality to a neighborhood. Finitely many such neighborhoods cover any smaller closed ball, giving finite global H_m members generating exactly I there.

Kernel convergence: mean-value bounds give bounded evaluations on compact subsets; Cauchy estimates uniformly bound derivatives of norm1 sections on smaller compacts. Therefore evaluation functionals ell_z∈H_m* vary continuously in operator norm. For an orthonormal basis f_l, Parseval gives K_m(z)=sum_l|f_l(z)|²=||ell_z||², finite continuous. Increasing continuous partial diagonal sums converge uniformly on compact sets by Dini. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds product tails by their diagonal tails, proving normal convergence of sum_l f_l(z)f_l*(w) on compact products, with the second factor the conjugate complex domain and f_l*(w)=overline(f_l(overline w)). This justifies the countable basis, evaluations and normally convergent tails; no infinite series is itself a finite witness.

Relative finite reduction at FIXED m: let E=closure B_a^2 and choose a concentric Stein ball E⊂⊂V⊂⊂D. Exact generation on a slightly larger compact ball provides finite H_m members generating I throughout V. Put their finite-dimensional span first in the orthonormal basis. A constant invertible change of basis preserves their ideal, so the first s basis members generate I on V.

On V×conjugate V let J be the coherent ideal generated by the s² products f_a(z)f_b*(w). It is exactly the product of the extended ideals from the two factors. Every finite partial kernel tail belongs to J at every stalk, because every f_l is locally a holomorphic combination of the first s in its factor. Closedness of coherent sections under compact convergence puts T_N=sum_(l>N)f_l(z)f_l*(w) in J(V×conjugate V). It tends to0 in compact-open topology and, by n1's proved topology identification, in the natural Fréchet topology.

The finite generating sheaf map O^(s²)→J has coherent kernel. The product is strongly1-complete, so Cartan B via the checked IX4.11 gives surjectivity on global sections. The coefficient map is continuous, hence open by Fréchet open mapping. Apply openness to the neighborhood requiring each coefficient to have supremum<delta/s on E×conjugate E. For sufficiently large N, T_N has coefficients a_ab,N in that neighborhood. On w=overline z,
0≤K_m-P_N=T_N(z,overline z)≤(delta/s)(sum_(a≤s)|f_a(z)|)^2≤delta sum_(a≤s)|f_a(z)|²≤delta P_N(z),
where P_N=sum_(l≤N)|f_l|². Positivity on the diagonal supplies the first inequality; the coefficient bound estimates absolute value, so complex signs are harmless. Consequently P_N≤K_m≤(1+delta)P_N throughout E, including common zeros. Its first s retain exact generation. N may depend arbitrarily on m,u. There is no uniform-in-m division estimate, generator-number bound or unproved log C_m/m control. Take delta=1.

Exact fixed-cover transfer: for x∈closure B_a^2∩closure B_b^2, compactness supplies uniformly positive-radius transfer balls inside B_a^3∩B_b^3. The finitely many chart transitions have uniformly bounded derivatives, inverses and volume ratios there. On a simply connected transfer ball rho_b-rho_a=Re t for holomorphic t. For F∈H_(m,a), choose a cutoff chi equal1 near x, supported in that ball, with uniform annular derivative bounds. Extend chi F exp(mt/2) by0 and solve its dbar on B_b^3 with
W_b=m(u+rho_b)+n log|z_b-z_b(x)|²+|z_b|².
On the data support the cancellation is EXACT:
|F exp(mt/2)|² exp(-m(u+rho_b))=|F|² exp(-m(u+rho_a)).
The holomorphic exponential has zero dbar derivative. Pole factors on the cutoff annulus, cutoff derivatives, coordinate Jacobians and quadratic factors are bounded geometrically. H bounds the solution norm by a geometric multiple of ||F||_(m,a)². Removing the added weight costs another geometric constant because the added function is bounded above on the entire destination ball. Near x the solution is holomorphic, and the pole exponent n forces h(x)=0 by the previous Taylor calculation with q=0. Local upper bounds for v_b suffice for vanishing; they need not enter any norm constant.

Thus F_b=chi F exp(mt/2)-h is holomorphic on the destination, F_b(x)=F(x)exp(mt(x)/2), and ||F_b||_(m,b)²≤C||F||_(m,a)² with C independent of m,u,x. Evaluation suprema give K_(m,b)≥C^(-1)exp(m(rho_b-rho_a))K_(m,a). Reverse the charts for the opposite direction. Therefore
C^(-1)K_(m,a)exp(-m rho_a)≤K_(m,b)exp(-m rho_b)≤C K_(m,a)exp(-m rho_a)
everywhere on inner overlaps. These are inequalities of finite nonnegative numbers, valid at zeros and forcing their common zero locus. Finite reduction changes ratios by at most2. Hence q_(m,a)=m^(-1)log P_(m,a)-rho_a have extended comparisons within D/m, D=log(2C); at finite values their absolute difference is at most D/m. No subtraction of infinities occurs.

O gives K_(m,a)(x)≥C_O^(-1)exp(m(u+rho_a)(x)) on closure B_a^2, with a geometric C_O≥1 common to the cover. At u(x)=-infinity this is the trivial nonnegative inequality. P≥K/2 gives q_(m,a)≥u-log(2C_O)/m. Set A=log(2C_O). Mean-value applied to |F|² on radius r, the estimate integral|F|²≤exp(m sup v_a)||F||², and the evaluation supremum yield
q_(m,a)(x)≤sup_(|z_a(y)-z_a(x)|<r)u(y)+M_rho r+(log C'+2n log(1/r))/m.
Here P≤K and smooth potential differences are bounded by M_rho r. The inequality holds locally uniformly at nearby points, with common chart margins. Shrink r so its numerator is positive. This uniformity is required before usc regularization.

Set the known beta_a=1-|z_a|²/(r_a^1)^2, nonnegative on B_a^1, zero at its boundary and at least3/4 on the cores. Choose L=4(D+1) and the permitted actual formula
Phi_m(x)=max_(a:x∈B_a^1){q_(m,a)(x)+(L beta_a(x)+A)/m}.
At a boundary point of B_a^1, a core B_b^0 contains it. On a small fixed neighborhood beta_b-beta_a≥1/2. Extended overlap comparison gives branch_b≥branch_a+(L/2-D)/m at finite values and domination everywhere, including common zeros. Since L/2-D=D+2>0, the boundary branch can be discarded there. This proves valid global gluing without a boundary current or discontinuity.

Each q branch satisfies theta+dd^c q=m^(-1)dd^c log P≥0. A known finite C_beta bounds all negative barrier Hessians by C_beta omega. Finite maxima preserve this common bound, giving theta+dd^c Phi_m≥-L C_beta omega/m. All finite tuples generate EXACTLY I(mu) near the required inner compact balls. Two-way local generator comparisons preserve that ideal-norm type under the maximum; the correction is the specified expression, never an arbitrary witness. Because beta≥0, A/m gives Phi_m≥u. A fixed small radius in the upper estimate bounds sup Phi_m by sup u plus geometry uniformly for m≥1; the lower supremum bound follows from Phi_m≥u. Choose a finite numeric B accordingly. Dependence of B and holomorphic tuples on u in this existence proof does not put u into the certificate tests.

For fixed x, sufficiently small r and every nearby y, uniform coordinate comparisons bound every active branch by
Phi_m(y)≤sup_(B(x,C1 r))u+C2 r+(C3+2n log(1/r)+A+L)/m.
Take the supremum over m_k≥m_j and then usc in y. The positive numerator is bounded by its value divided by m_j. The envelope proof of n2 legitimizes the tail and its curvature. Let j→infinity, then r↓0. Usc of canonical u makes the upper bound tend to u(x), even at a pole, where every finite upper threshold holds throughout a sufficiently small neighborhood. Conversely every Phi_m≥u, so every usc tail is ≥u pointwise. Therefore Psi_j↓u EXACTLY at every finite and polar point.

Take m_j=2^j and epsilon_j=(L C_beta+1)/m_j. Curvature/supremum checks hold and the tuples generate the prescribed A_(m_j)=I(m_j u). Apply n2's exact capped integral identity with this exact tail limit. It gives certificate compatibility for EVERY real c>0 and every germ with exactly the local U/C quantifiers. No strong openness, mass assumption or integer-to-real extension is used. This proves R and necessity; with n2 it proves the precise general iff theorem.

notes.summary: P¹ critical thresholds and zero-mass certificates verified; direct Cantor/Jensen proof gives identical all-real unit ideals with raw masses[0,1]. Frozen smaller-exponent formula FAIL; corrected formula is conditional.

On P¹, omega=dd^c log(1+|z|²) has density pi^(-1)(1+|z|²)^(-2) times planar area and integral1; integration to radius R gives R²/(1+R²). G=log|z|²-log(1+|z|²) has omega+dd^c G=delta_0 and sup G=0. For0≤a≤1, u=aG has positive current (1-a)omega+a delta_0. A nonzero germ at0 of order k is integrable against exp(-cu) iff integral_0^t r^(2k-2ac+1)dr is finite, iff k>ac-1, iff k≥floor(ac). At integer ac the k=ac-1 integral diverges logarithmically. Thus I(cu)=O(-floor(ac){0}) for ALL real c, including critical thresholds; elsewhere stalks are units.

For m≥1 let q_m=floor(am). The finite tuple sqrt(binomial(m-q_m,l))z^(q_m+l),0≤l≤m-q_m, generates (z^q_m). Its squared sum is |z|^(2q_m)(1+|z|²)^(m-q_m), so its corrected logarithm is Phi_m=(q_m/m)G. In w=1/z use sqrt(binomial(m-q_m,l))w^l, containing1; the corrected expression is -(q_m/m)log(1+|w|²), the same global function. Restrict these agreeing formulas to fixed bounded nested chart balls whose cores cover P¹; L=A=0 is allowed. Their current is (1-q_m/m)omega+(q_m/m)delta_0≥0 and their suprema are0.

For dyadic m, q_(2m)≥2q_m and q_m/m≤q_(2m)/(2m)≤a, while0≤a-q_m/m<1/m. Coefficients increase to a and G≤0, so Phi_j↓aG. If a>0 the coefficient becomes positive after finitely many scales, giving the exact pole value at0; if a=0 its expression is defined through the unit tuple as0 everywhere, without0 times-infinity. The n2 capped identity proves full-real compatibility. At a=1 every norm is G; on its finite locus the current delta_0 vanishes, so degree-one nonpluripolar truncations give mass0. Separately, background theta=0 with V_0=0 and global unit norms has unit ideals and mass0. The smooth a=0 example in the positive omega background instead has mass1. No mass division is made.

Three incompatible arrays: O(-D) for c<1 and units for c≥1 violates A_d⊂A_c for d>c, which follows by normalizing u locally to≤0 and comparing exponential weights. Units for c<1 and O(-D) for c≥1 have A_2=(z), A_1²=(z²), violating DEL subadditivity. O(-(ceil(c)-1)D) satisfies monotonicity and subadditivity because ceil(c+d)≥ceil(c)+ceil(d)-1, but1 belongs at c=1 and at no c=1+delta; strong openness excludes it. DEL/SO are disclosed published auxiliary imports, not directly validated original editions here. Adding a smooth local theta-potential makes weights psh, and bounded changes preserve all involved ideals. These are necessary obstructions, not a finite sufficient axiom list; n2 implies none can have a certificate.

For the raw obstruction, start with[0,1], ell_0=1 and ell_k=exp(-4^k). Place two next-level endpoint intervals inside each level-k interval;2ell_(k+1)<ell_k. Their intersection F is compact and carries Bernoulli probability mu assigning each level-k interval mass2^(-k). It has no atoms because a point's enclosing masses tend to0, and F has planar area0. For x∈F its containing interval gives mass at least2^(-k) within distance ell_k. For t∈[4^(k-1),4^k], exp(-t)≥ell_k. Layer-cake therefore gives integral -log|x-p|dmu(p)≥sum_(k≥1)(4^k-4^(k-1))2^(-k)=sum_(k≥1)3*2^(k-2)=infinity.

The squared chordal kernel G_p(z)=log(|z-p|²/((1+|z|²)(1+|p|²))) is≤0, has omega+dd^c G_p=delta_p and sup0. Rotation invariance gives integral_P¹(-G_p)omega=1 uniformly in p; reduce to p=0 and substitute t=r²/(1+r²). Fubini/Tonelli thus gives V=integral G_p dmu in L¹ and omega+dd^c V=mu distributionally. Reverse Fatou under the common upper bound0 proves usc of the actual integral. On a local chart, integrate sub-mean for G_p+rho; uniform local L¹ bounds justify interchange. Consequently V+rho is psh and the integral is its exact canonical value. V is finite and smooth away from compact F and equals-infinity on F by layer-cake and bounded chordal corrections. Its pole set is exactly F, proving polarity without a capacity theorem.

For0≤s≤1 put u_s=sV, defining u_0=0. Its current is (1-s)omega+s mu. Fix real c>0 and x with cs>0. Nonatomicity supplies a small coordinate disk whose doubled disk has mu-mass beta<1/(cs). The far potential is bounded below on the smaller disk; chordal/smooth corrections are bounded. If beta>0, Jensen with probability mu_near/beta gives
exp(-cs integral log|z-p|²dmu_near(p))≤beta^(-1) integral|z-p|^(-2cs beta)dmu_near(p).
Truncation of the negative logarithm justifies the singular values. The right side has finite area integral uniformly in p because its radial exponent1-2cs beta>-1. Tonelli proves local exponential integrability. If beta=0 the near contribution is absent; if cs=0 the weight is1. Hence I(cu_s)=O for EVERY c and s.

For s>0 the finite locus is P¹ minus F, where u_s is smooth and its current is (1-s)omega. The degree-one nonpluripolar definition is the increasing limit of1_{u_s>-k}(omega+dd^c max(u_s,-k)). On that open set it is1_{u_s>-k}(1-s)omega. Boundary measures are discarded by the strict indicator. The union is the finite locus, and F has area0, so the product is (1-s)omega and mass1-s. At s=0 mass is1. One identical full-real unit array therefore contains every raw mass in[0,1], including0. Normalization by subtracting sup changes neither ideals nor mass; V is nonconstant, so scaled normalized representatives differ. Raw representatives and mass do not descend. Distinct P-envelopes would additionally require a P-envelope mass-preservation theorem and are not inferred here.
